items.title: RBA warns of 'rough' time ahead as interest rates rise by 0.25pc to 4.35pc
items.description: The RBA lifts rates by 0.25 basis points to 4.35 per cent, which fully unwinds last year's rate cuts. But governor Michele Bullock says the rate rises will not stop higher inflation heading Australia's way from the Iran war.

items.title: Five things you can do to save money now that interest rates have gone up
items.description: Sensible Emily untangles the latest interest rate decision and gives you tips to help you save money.

items.title: Hegseth says ceasefire 'is not over', with US 'not looking for fight'
items.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the ceasefire with Iran is still in effect, despite the US and Iran launching attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. Read how developments on Tuesday April 5 unfolded.

items.title: Labor axes funding for $45b Inland Rail project linking Melbourne to Brisbane
items.description: The federal government has halted plans for the Melbourne to Brisbane Inland Rail, amid concerns the project could cost more than $45 billion to complete.

items.title: 'Police can't help you': The threat issued to Melbourne's pub and club owners
items.description: Melbourne is in the grip of a crime wave. But this time it's different and pub and club owners say they are scared as 'The Cartel' issues threats they do not understand.

items.title: 'I have lost basically everything': Ex-AFL player opens up on compensation fight
items.description: Head trauma ended Aiden O'Driscoll's promising AFL career before he could play his first game. Now, like many former footballers affected by brain injuries, he faces an uncertain future as he fights for compensation.

items.title: Indigenous commissioner condemns comedian's 'deeply offensive' video
items.description: South Australia's Commissioner for Aboriginal Children and Young People speaks out against a "deeply offensive" social media video posted by comedian Alex "Shooter" Williamson in the wake of the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby.

items.title: One-off tax cut in play as Albanese keeps budget options open
items.description: A one-off tax break for working Australians remains a live option for cost-of-living relief as Labor finalises plans for next week's federal budget.

items.title: Firefighter pulled knife on Jewish paramedic, royal commission told
items.description: Paramedic Joshua Gomperts tells the royal commission into antisemitism how a firefighter pulled a hunting knife on him during a music festival in regional Victoria.

items.title: Singapore approves caning for school bullies
items.description: The move is part of Singapore's new anti-bullying measures introduced by the Ministry of Education.

items.title: Meteor shower, a comet and the Moon: What's in the sky tonight
items.description: The Moon will outshine May's annual meteor shower, but there are other things to look for in the sky including a beautiful comet.

items.title: Blast at fireworks factory in China kills at least 26, state media says
items.description: Authorities evacuated nearby residents and deployed rescue robots after the deadly explosion at the fireworks factory in Hunan province.

items.title: Human-to-human transmission suspected in deadly hantavirus outbreak
items.description: The World Health Organization says no rats were found on board the cruise vessel where the outbreak has taken hold, with three people having died of confirmed or suspected infections of the rat-borne virus.

items.title: Met gala red carpet: How the stars interpreted 'fashion is art' dress code
items.description: A quick glance at the outfits from one of the fashion world's biggest events of the year.

items.title: I don't care if I confuse people. Being 'wasian' is who I am
items.description: Being biracial or "wasian" (that is, both white and Asian) is a unique experience. There are lots of things I share with both Asian and white people, but there are experiences novel to being wasian.

items.title: Australia is experiencing HRT menopause patch shortages. Here's why
items.description: Supplies of some HRT patches may not return to normal until at least the end of the year. So what can patients do if they're impacted by shortages?

items.title: For these dads, a night at the pub includes crash course in hair styling
items.description: The viral social media trend encouraging dads to learn how to style their daughters' hair is challenging gender roles.

items.title: Surfers Paradise ditches cars for pedestrians as esplanade closed for good
items.description: The Gold Coast council has voted to permanently close part of the Surfers Paradise Esplanade despite division over traffic and business impacts.

items.title: Romania's pro-EU government collapses after no-confidence vote
items.description: The country's currency falls to a record low against the euro as concerns mount about the state of its finances.

items.title: Carlton fined $75,000 over Elijah Hollands incident
items.description: Three weeks on from Elijah Hollands's mental health episode at the MCG, the AFL fines Carlton $75,000 for its handling of the player and issues around the incident.

items.title: 'Scapegoating': Staff, students and politicians back ANU interim leader
items.description: A group of politicians, unionists, students and staff come together to support the Australian National University's interim leader, expressing concerns she is being scapegoated for existing turmoil within the embattled institution.

items.title: Students vent frustrations over Notre Dame nursing training
items.description: Numerous nursing students at Perth's Notre Dame University say issues with work placement have left them wondering if they will be able to graduate on time.

items.title: Daughter 'scared' for mother appearing at antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Natalie Levy had an idyllic childhood growing up singing songs on Bondi Beach, but her children now attend school surrounded by heavy security and swastikas graffitied on buildings.

items.title: '24/7 wanding searches' of patients in hospital's behavioural assessment unit
items.description: Patients entering Canberra Hospital's Behavioural Assessment Unit will now undergo metal detector screening after a knife incident forced staff into a three-hour lockdown.

items.title: Who are the winners and losers in Victoria's budget?
items.description: Despite rising debt, the Victorian government has found money for hip-pocket measures and a justice system overhaul. These are some of the winners and losers from the 2026-27 budget.
